The full suite is green: **258 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors**.

## Summary

The change is to reject creating an owner when another owner already has the **same last name and same telephone number**, responding with 409.

The endpoint's POST pipeline (`owners.POST.yml`) already wired a `EnsureOwnerUnique` step and a `OwnerAlreadyExistsException` → 409 handler. The only change needed was to relax the duplicate rule in `EnsureOwnerUnique` — it previously required all five fields (first name, last name, address, city, telephone) to match. I changed it to match on **last name + telephone**:

- `EnsureOwnerUnique.java` — now iterates `findByLastName(...)` and throws `OwnerAlreadyExistsException` (→ 409) when an existing owner shares the same last name and telephone.
- `OwnerAlreadyExistsException.java` — updated the doc comment to reflect the new rule.

The `Cp02Tests` acceptance tests confirm the behavior: same last name + telephone → 409; same last name but different telephone → 2xx.
